In an emergency, if truly necessary, the control may be handed over to the border inspection station first, and the control procedures may be completed afterwards.

Article 405 For evidentiary materials originating from outside the territory of China, the People's Court shall examine the source of the materials, the provider, the time of provision, the person who obtained them, and the time of obtaining, among other things. After examination, if such materials can prove the facts of the case and comply with the provisions of the Criminal Procedure Law, they may be used as evidence, except where the provider or a bilateral treaty concluded between China and the relevant country imposes explicit restrictions on the scope of use; if the source of the materials is unknown or their authenticity cannot be confirmed, they shall not be used as the basis for deciding the case.
If a party, his or her defender, or litigation agent provides evidentiary materials from outside the territory of China, such materials shall be notarized by a notary office of the country where they are located, authenticated by the central foreign affairs authority or its authorized organ of that country, and authenticated by the embassy or consulate of China in that country.

Article 406 For a foreign-related criminal case that meets the requirements of Article 202, paragraph 1, and Article 232 of the Criminal Procedure Law, the trial period may be extended upon approval or decision of the relevant People's Court.

Article 407 After the judgment of a foreign-related criminal case is pronounced, if the embassy or consulate of the country of nationality of a foreign party requests to be provided with the judgment document, the request may be submitted to the Higher People's Court in the locality of the People's Court trying the case, and the People's Court may provide it.

Article 408 In accordance with international treaties concluded or acceded to by the People's Republic of China, or on the basis of the principle of reciprocity, the People's Court and foreign courts may request criminal judicial assistance from each other.
If the matter requested by a foreign court is detrimental to the sovereignty, security, or public interests of the People's Republic of China, the People's Court shall not provide assistance.

Article 409 Requests for and provision of judicial assistance shall be made through the channels prescribed by the international treaties concluded or acceded to by the People's Republic of China; if no treaty relationship exists, it shall be done through diplomatic channels.

Article 410 If a People's Court requests a foreign country to provide judicial assistance, it shall be reviewed by the Higher People's Court and then reported to the Supreme People's Court for examination and approval.
If a foreign court requests China to provide judicial assistance and the matter falls within the functions and powers of the People's Court, it shall be transmitted to the relevant People's Court for handling after examination and approval by the Supreme People's Court.

Article 411 A letter of request submitted by the People's Court to a foreign country for judicial assistance and the attached documents shall be accompanied by a translation in the language of that country or a text in another language as prescribed by an international treaty.
A letter of request submitted by a foreign court to China for judicial assistance and the attached documents shall be accompanied by a Chinese translation or a text in another language as prescribed by an international treaty.

Article 413 If the People's Court serves criminal litigation documents through diplomatic channels on a recipient residing outside the territory of the People's Republic of China, the documents to be served shall be reviewed by the Higher People's Court and then reported to the Supreme People's Court for examination. If the Supreme People's Court considers that the documents may be sent, it shall hand them over to the competent department of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for transmission.
If a foreign court requests the People's Court to serve criminal litigation documents through diplomatic channels, the embassy of that country in China shall hand over the legal documents to the competent department of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of China for transmission to the Supreme People's Court. After examination, if the Supreme People's Court considers that the matter falls within the functions and powers of the People's Court and can be served on behalf, it shall transmit the documents to the relevant People's Court for handling.
Article 414 Other matters arising during the trial of a foreign-related criminal case shall be handled in accordance with laws, judicial interpretations, and other relevant provisions.

Article 415 If a criminal who is sentenced to death with a two-year reprieve commits an intentional crime during the period of reprieve, the case shall be tried by the Intermediate People's Court in the place where the criminal is serving the sentence according to law, and the judgment rendered may be appealed or protested.
After the judgment or ruling finding the intentional crime is established and becomes legally effective, it shall be reported level by level to the Supreme People's Court for approval of execution of the death penalty.

Article 416 The period of a death sentence with a two-year reprieve shall be calculated from the date on which the legal document approving the death sentence with a two-year reprieve is pronounced or served.
Upon the expiration of the period of the death sentence with a two-year reprieve, if the penalty shall be commuted according to law, the People's Court shall promptly commute the sentence. If the death sentence with a two-year reprieve is commuted to life imprisonment or fixed-term imprisonment upon expiration, the term of imprisonment shall be calculated from the date on which the period of the reprieve expires.

Article 417 The execution order for the death penalty issued by the Supreme People's Court shall be transmitted by the Higher People's Court to the People's Court of first instance for execution. Upon receiving the execution order, the People's Court of first instance shall execute it within seven days.
If an intentional crime is committed during the period of a death sentence with a two-year reprieve and the Supreme People's Court approves the execution of the death penalty, the execution shall be carried out by the Intermediate People's Court in the place where the criminal is serving the sentence.

Article 419 If, after the execution order for the death penalty is issued but before execution, the Supreme People's Court discovers any of the circumstances specified in paragraph 1 of the preceding article, it shall immediately rule to suspend the execution of the death penalty and transfer the relevant materials to the lower People's Court.

Article 420 After receiving the Supreme People's Court's ruling to suspend the execution of the death penalty, the lower People's Court shall, together with relevant departments, investigate and verify the reasons for the suspension, and promptly report the investigation results and opinions level by level to the Supreme People's Court for review.

Article 421 The investigation results and opinions submitted by the lower People's Court regarding the suspension of execution of the death penalty shall be reviewed by the collegial panel of the Supreme People's Court that originally rendered the judgment or ruling approving the death penalty. If necessary, a separate collegial panel shall be formed for review.

Article 423 Before executing the death penalty, the People's Court of first instance shall inform the criminal of the right to meet with his or her close relatives. If the criminal applies for a meeting and provides specific contact information, the People's Court shall notify his or her close relatives. If the close relatives of the criminal apply for a meeting, the People's Court shall permit it and promptly arrange the meeting.

Article 424 The Primary People's Court that tried the case shall, three days before the execution of the death penalty, notify the People's Procuratorate at the same level to designate an officer to supervise the execution on site.

Article 425 The death penalty shall be executed by means of shooting, injection, or other methods.
Where the death penalty is executed by injection, it shall be executed at a designated execution ground or within a detention facility.
Where the death penalty is executed by methods other than shooting or injection, prior approval from the Supreme People's Court shall be obtained through report by levels.

Article 426 Before the execution of the death penalty, the judicial officer directing the execution shall verify the identity of the criminal, ask whether he or she has any dying words or letters, and make a record thereof, and then deliver the criminal to the executing officers for execution of the death penalty.
The execution of the death penalty shall be announced, and parading the criminal in public or any other act that humiliates the personality of the criminal is prohibited.

Article 427 After the execution of the death penalty, a forensic medical examiner shall verify that the criminal is indeed dead, and the court clerk present shall make a record. The People's Court responsible for the execution shall, within fifteen days after the execution of the death penalty, report the execution circumstances, including photos of the criminal before and after the execution of the death penalty, to the Supreme People's Court.

Article 429 Where a criminal sentenced to death with a two-year reprieve, life imprisonment, fixed-term imprisonment, or criminal detention is in custody when handed over for execution, the Primary People's Court shall, within ten days after the judgment or ruling takes effect, deliver the judgment, ruling, copy of the bill of prosecution, copy of the private prosecution complaint, execution notice, and case closure registration form to the detention center, and the public security organ shall hand over the criminal for execution.
Where a criminal needs to be taken into custody to serve the sentence but was not held in custody before the judgment or ruling took effect, the People's Court shall, based on the effective judgment or ruling, deliver the criminal to the detention center for custody, and handle the execution procedures in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph.

Article 430 In a case tried jointly, where some defendants are sentenced to death and other co-defendants who are not sentenced to death need to be held in custody to serve their sentences, execution shall be carried out within ten days after their judgments or rulings take effect. However, if such a co-defendant participated in the commission of the crime for which the death penalty is imposed, execution shall be carried out after the Supreme People's Court has reviewed and interrogated the defendant sentenced to death.
Article 431 The receipt of the execution notice, after being stamped by the detention center, shall be attached to the case file for reference.

Article 432 Where a criminal sentenced to life imprisonment, fixed-term imprisonment, or criminal detention meets the conditions specified in paragraphs 1 and 2 of Article 254 of the Criminal Procedure Law, and the People's Court decides to grant temporary service of sentence outside prison, it shall issue a decision on temporary service of sentence outside prison, specifying the basic information of the criminal, the crime and penalty determined by the judgment, the reasons and legal basis for the decision on temporary service of sentence outside prison, etc., notify the judicial administrative organ at the county level where the criminal resides to send personnel to handle the transfer procedures, and serve a copy of the decision on temporary service of sentence outside prison to the People's Procuratorate and the public security organ at the county level where the criminal resides.
Where the People's Procuratorate considers the People's Court's decision on temporary service of sentence outside prison to be improper and submits a written opinion within the statutory time limit, the People's Court shall immediately re-examine the decision and make a decision within one month.

Article 434 The People's Court shall deliver the decision on execution in prison to the judicial administrative organ at the county level where the criminal resides, which shall hand over the criminal for execution in accordance with relevant provisions. The decision on execution in prison shall also be served simultaneously to the People's Procuratorate and the public security organ at the same level where the criminal resides.

Article 435 Where a criminal subject to execution in prison has circumstances that shall not be counted into the term of imprisonment served, the People's Court shall, at the time of making the decision on execution in prison, determine the specific period that shall not be counted into the term of imprisonment served.

Article 436 For a criminal sentenced to public surveillance or placed on probation, the People's Court shall verify his or her place of residence. At the time of pronouncement of judgment, the court shall inform the criminal in writing of the time limit for reporting to the judicial administrative organ at the county level of his or her place of residence and the consequences of failing to report on time. Within ten days after the judgment or ruling takes effect, the court shall serve the judgment, ruling, execution notice, and other legal documents to the judicial administrative organ at the county level where the criminal resides, and at the same time serve a copy to the People's Procuratorate at the county level where the criminal resides.

Article 437 For a criminal sentenced solely to deprivation of political rights, the People's Court shall, within ten days after the judgment or ruling takes effect, serve the judgment, ruling, execution notice, and other legal documents to the public security organ at the county level where the criminal resides, and serve a copy to the People's Procuratorate at the county level where the criminal resides.
Article 438 The execution of pecuniary penalties and incidental civil judgments shall be carried out by the organ responsible for the execution of judgments and rulings of the Primary People's Court.

Article 439 A fine shall be paid in a lump sum or in installments within the period specified in the judgment. If the fine is not paid or is not paid in full without just cause upon expiration of the period, the People's Court shall enforce payment. If the fine still cannot be fully paid after enforcement, at any time, including after the principal punishment has been executed, if property of the person subject to enforcement is found to be available for execution, the amount shall be recovered.
Where an administrative authority has already imposed a fine on the defendant for the same facts, when the People's Court imposes a fine, it shall offset the amount and deduct the portion already executed as an administrative penalty.
Where confiscation of property is imposed, execution shall be carried out immediately after the judgment takes effect.

Article 440 In the process of executing pecuniary penalties and incidental civil judgments, if a person not involved in the case raises an objection to the ownership of the property subject to execution, the People's Court shall review and handle the matter by reference to the provisions on execution objections in civil litigation.

Article 441 Where a person subject to enforcement is sentenced to a pecuniary penalty and at the same time bears incidental civil compensation liability, he or she shall first perform the civil compensation liability.
Where a person subject to enforcement owes legitimate debts before the imposition of the pecuniary penalty that need to be repaid with the property subject to execution, such debts shall be repaid upon the request of the creditor.

Article 442 Where the person subject to enforcement or the property subject to execution is located in another place, execution may be entrusted to the local People's Court.
After executing a pecuniary penalty, the entrusted court shall promptly turn over the executed property to the state treasury.

Article 445 Where a pecuniary penalty is wholly or partially revoked, the property already executed shall be wholly or partially returned to the person subject to enforcement; if return is impossible, compensation shall be made in accordance with law.

Article 446 Where a person subject to enforcement applies for reduction or exemption of a fine due to genuine difficulty in paying the fine caused by irresistible disaster, he or she shall submit relevant supporting materials. The People's Court shall make a ruling within one month after receiving the application. If the statutory conditions for reduction or exemption are met, the application shall be granted; if not, the application shall be rejected.

Article 447 Where this Interpretation does not provide for the execution of pecuniary penalties and incidental civil judgments, the relevant provisions on civil execution shall be applied by reference.

Article 448 Where a criminal sentenced to death with a two-year reprieve commits no intentional crime during the period of the reprieve, after the expiration of the reprieve period, a ruling shall be made to commute the sentence; if the criminal commits a new crime after the expiration of the reprieve period but before a ruling on commutation is made, the sentence shall be commuted in accordance with law and a separate trial shall be conducted for the new crime.

Article 451 When trying a case of commutation of punishment or parole, the execution of pecuniary penalties and incidental civil judgments, as well as the criminal's restitution of stolen property or compensation for losses, shall be examined. Where the criminal actively performs the obligations determined by the judgment, he or she may be found to have demonstrated repentance and shall be treated leniently in commutation of punishment or parole; where he or she has the ability to perform but fails to do so, he or she shall be treated strictly in commutation of punishment or parole.

Article 454 After making a ruling on commutation of punishment or parole, the People's Court shall, within seven days, serve the ruling on the executing authority that requested the commutation or parole, the People's Procuratorate at the same level, and the criminal himself or herself. Where the People's Procuratorate considers the ruling on commutation or parole to be improper and submits a written correction opinion within the statutory time limit, the People's Court shall, after receiving the opinion, form a new collegial panel to try the case and make a ruling within one month.

Article 455 Before a ruling on commutation of punishment or parole is made, if the executing authority submits a written request to withdraw the recommendation for commutation or parole, whether to grant the request shall be decided by the People's Court.

Article 456 Where a People's Court discovers that a ruling on commutation of punishment or parole made by itself that has already taken effect is indeed erroneous, it shall form a new collegial panel to retry the case; where it discovers that a ruling on commutation of punishment or parole made by a lower People's Court that has already taken effect is indeed erroneous, it may instruct the lower People's Court to form a new collegial panel to retry the case.

Article 457 Where a criminal on probation or parole commits a new crime during the probation or parole period, or it is discovered that he or she has other crimes not yet adjudicated before the judgment was pronounced, and the probation or parole shall be revoked, the People's Court trying the new crime shall revoke the probation or parole declared in the original judgment or ruling, and notify the original trial court and the executing authority in writing.

Article 459 When trying juvenile criminal cases, the People's Court shall implement the policy of education, persuasion, and rescue, adhere to the principle of giving priority to education and taking punishment as supplementary, and strengthen special protection for juveniles.

Article 460 The People's Court shall strengthen contacts with relevant government departments and organizations such as the Communist Youth League, Women's Federation, Trade Union, and juvenile protection organizations, promote the work of people's jurors in juvenile criminal cases, situation investigation, placement and assistance, and education, fully protect the legitimate rights and interests of juveniles, and actively participate in the comprehensive management of social order.

Article 461 Juvenile criminal cases shall be tried by judicial officers who are familiar with the physical and psychological characteristics of juveniles and skilled in conducting ideological education work for juveniles, and the relative stability of the work of such judicial officers shall be maintained.
People's jurors in juvenile criminal cases shall generally be staff members of units such as the Communist Youth League, Women's Federation, Trade Union, schools, juvenile protection organizations, or retired personnel from relevant units, who are familiar with the physical and psychological characteristics of juveniles, enthusiastic about the work of educating, persuading, and rescuing misguided juveniles, and have received necessary training.

Article 462 Intermediate People's Courts and Primary People's Courts may establish independent juvenile case adjudication divisions. Where conditions are not yet available, a collegial panel for juvenile criminal cases shall be established within the criminal adjudication division, or designated persons shall be responsible for trying juvenile criminal cases. Higher People's Courts shall establish a collegial panel for juvenile criminal cases within the criminal adjudication division. Where conditions permit, independent juvenile case adjudication divisions may be established.
Juvenile case adjudication divisions and collegial panels for juvenile criminal cases are collectively referred to as juvenile courts.

Article 463 The following cases shall be tried by the juvenile court:
(1) Cases where the defendant was under eighteen years of age when committing the alleged crime and under twenty years of age when the People's Court dockets the case;
(2) Joint crime cases where the defendant was under eighteen years of age when committing the alleged crime and under twenty years of age when the People's Court dockets the case, and is alleged to be the principal culprit or principal offender.
Where other joint crime cases involve juvenile defendants, or other criminal cases involving juveniles, whether they shall be tried by the juvenile court shall be decided by the president of the court based on the actual circumstances of the juvenile court's work.

Article 464 Where a joint crime case involving juveniles and adults is prosecuted in separate indictments to the same People's Court, it may be tried by the same adjudication organization; where it is inappropriate to be tried by the same adjudication organization, it may be tried separately by the juvenile court and the criminal adjudication division.
Where a joint crime case involving juveniles and adults is tried separately by different People's Courts or different adjudication organizations, the relevant People's Courts or adjudication organizations shall keep each other informed of the trial circumstances of the defendants in the joint crime, and pay attention to the balance of sentencing for the entire case.

Article 465 For juvenile criminal cases, where necessary, the higher People's Court may, in accordance with Article 26 of the Criminal Procedure Law, designate a lower People's Court to transfer the case to another People's Court for trial.

Article 466 When trying a juvenile criminal case, the People's Court shall, during interrogation and court session, notify the legal representative of the juvenile defendant to be present. If the legal representative cannot be notified, cannot be present, or is a co-defendant, other adult relatives of the juvenile defendant, representatives from the school, work unit, grassroots organization of the place of residence, or juvenile protection organization may also be notified to be present, and the relevant circumstances shall be recorded in the case file.
Other persons present may, in addition to exercising the rights provided in paragraph 2 of Article 270 of the Criminal Procedure Law in accordance with law, participate in the court education of the juvenile defendant and other work with the consent of the court.
Where summary procedure is applied to try a juvenile criminal case, the provisions of the preceding two paragraphs shall apply.
The provisions of paragraphs 1 and 2 shall apply to the questioning of juvenile victims and witnesses.

Article 467: Cases where the defendant is under the age of 18 at the time of trial shall not be heard in public. With the consent of the minor defendant and his or her legal representative, representatives from the minor's school and the organization for the protection of minors may be present. The number and scope of representatives present shall be determined by the court. Representatives present may, with the consent of the court, participate in the court's educational work concerning the minor defendant.
For cases that are heard in public according to law but may require sealing of criminal records, no personnel shall be organized to observe the hearing.

Article 468: Where it is truly necessary to notify a minor victim or witness to testify in court, the People's Court shall take corresponding protective measures based on the circumstances of the case. Where conditions permit, methods such as video may be used to examine their statements or testimony.

Article 469: When hearing a criminal case involving a minor, the name, address, photograph, and other information that may lead to the identification of the minor shall not be disclosed to the public.
Case files of criminal cases involving minors that have been consulted, excerpted, or reproduced shall not be made public or disseminated.
The provisions of the preceding two paragraphs shall apply to criminal cases where the victim is a minor.
Article 470: Where this Chapter does not provide for matters arising from the hearing of criminal cases involving minors, the relevant provisions of this Interpretation shall apply.

Article 471: When serving a copy of the indictment on a minor defendant, the People's Court shall explain to him or her the alleged crime and relevant legal provisions, and shall inform him or her of the trial procedure and the litigation rights and obligations.

Article 472: Where a minor defendant who is under the age of 18 at the time of trial has not retained a defender, the People's Court shall notify a legal aid institution to appoint a lawyer to provide defense for him or her.

Article 473: Where a minor victim or his or her legal representative has not retained a litigation agent due to financial difficulties or other reasons, the People's Court shall assist them in applying for legal aid.

Article 474: For a criminal case involving a minor, where the People's Court decides to apply the summary procedure, it shall seek the opinions of the minor defendant, his or her legal representative, and the defender. If any of the above persons objects, the summary procedure shall not be applied.

Article 475: Where the defendant was under the age of 18 when committing the alleged crime but has reached the age of 18 but not yet 20 at the time of trial, the People's Court shall, when holding the trial, generally notify his or her close relatives to be present in court. With the consent of the court, the close relatives may express opinions. If the close relatives cannot be notified, cannot be present, or are accomplices, this shall be recorded in the case file.

Article 476: The court shall accept the investigation reports transferred by the People's Procuratorate concerning the minor defendant's personality traits, family circumstances, social interactions, growth experience, causes of the crime, conduct before and after the crime, guardianship and education, and the written materials submitted by the defender reflecting the above circumstances of the minor defendant.
Where necessary, the People's Court may entrust the judicial administrative authority at the county level of the minor defendant's place of residence, the Communist Youth League organization, or other social organizations to investigate the above circumstances of the minor defendant, or may conduct the investigation itself.

Article 477: With respect to a criminal case involving a minor, the People's Court may, based on the circumstances, provide psychological counseling to the minor defendant; with the consent of the minor defendant and his or her legal representative, it may also conduct a psychological assessment of the minor defendant.

Article 478: Before the trial and during adjournment, the court may, based on the circumstances, arrange for the minor defendant to meet with his or her legal representative or other adult relatives or representatives as specified in Article 270, paragraph 1, of the Criminal Procedure Law.

Article 479: The People's Court shall set up seats for the minor defendant's legal representative or other adult relatives or representatives as specified in Article 270, paragraph 1, of the Criminal Procedure Law on the side of the defense table that is close to the public seating area.
When hearing a criminal case involving a minor that may result in a sentence of fixed-term imprisonment of less than five years or a negligent crime, the court may arrange the seats in a manner suitable for the characteristics of minors.

Article 480: Restraints shall not be used on a minor defendant in court, unless the defendant poses a high personal danger that may disrupt the trial proceedings. Where restraints must be used, they shall be discontinued immediately after the real danger is eliminated.

Article 481: Where a minor defendant or his or her legal representative refuses the defense of the defender in court, the provisions of Article 254, paragraphs 1 and 2, of this Interpretation shall apply.
Where, after the trial resumes, the minor defendant or his or her legal representative again refuses the defense of the defender in court, such refusal shall not be permitted. If the defendant has reached the age of 18 when the trial resumes, such refusal may be permitted, but he or she shall not retain another defender or request the appointment of another lawyer, and shall conduct his or her own defense.

Article 482: During the court proceedings, the judicial personnel shall, based on the intellectual development level and psychological state of the minor defendant, use language expressions suitable for minors.
Where it is discovered that there are instances of inducing a confession, reprimanding, ridiculing, or threatening the minor defendant, the presiding judge shall stop such conduct.

Article 483: Where the prosecution and defense propose sentencing recommendations such as public surveillance or probation for a minor defendant, they shall provide the court with written materials demonstrating that the minor defendant can obtain guardianship, assistance and education, and that there will be no significant adverse impact on the community in which he or she resides.

Article 484: The court shall examine the investigation reports concerning the minor defendant's circumstances and the written materials submitted by the defender regarding the minor defendant's circumstances, and shall hear the opinions of both the prosecution and the defense. The above reports and materials may serve as references for court education and sentencing.

Article 485: After the court debate concludes, the court may, based on the circumstances of the case, provide education to the minor defendant; where the minor defendant is found guilty, the court shall, after pronouncing the judgment, provide education to the minor defendant.
For the education of the minor defendant, the court may invite litigation participants, other adult relatives and representatives as specified in Article 270, paragraph 1, of the Criminal Procedure Law, as well as social investigators, psychological counselors, and others to participate.
For cases tried under the summary procedure, the provisions of the preceding two paragraphs shall apply to the court education of the minor defendant.
Article 486: After the minor defendant makes a final statement, the court shall inquire of his or her legal representative whether he or she wishes to make a supplementary statement.

Article 487: The pronouncement of judgment in a criminal case involving a minor shall be conducted in public, but shall not take the form of a public meeting or the like.
For cases where criminal records shall be sealed according to law, when the judgment is pronounced, no personnel shall be organized to observe the hearing; if there are observers, they shall be informed that they must not disseminate information about the case.

Article 488: In a criminal case involving a minor where judgment is to be pronounced on a scheduled date, if the minor defendant's legal representative cannot be notified, cannot be present in court, or is an accomplice, the court may notify other adult relatives or representatives as specified in Article 270, paragraph 1, of the Criminal Procedure Law to be present in court, and shall serve the judgment on the minor defendant's adult relatives after the pronouncement.

Article 489: When sending a minor offender to prison for execution of punishment or to community correction, the People's Court shall deliver the investigation report concerning the minor offender and the materials on his or her conduct during the trial, together with the relevant legal documents, to the executing authority.

Article 490: The criminal records of a minor who was under the age of 18 at the time of the crime and was sentenced to a punishment of fixed-term imprisonment of less than five years or exempted from criminal punishment shall be sealed.
Where cases concluded before December 31, 2012 meet the provisions of the preceding paragraph, the relevant criminal records shall also be sealed.
Where a judicial authority or a relevant entity applies to the People's Court to access sealed criminal records, it shall provide the reasons and basis for the access. The People's Court shall promptly make a decision on whether to grant the access application.

Article 491: The People's Court may establish contact with juvenile offender correctional institutions and other places of imprisonment to learn about the rehabilitation of minor offenders, assist in the work of assistance, education, and reform, and may conduct return visits and inspections of minor offenders currently serving their sentences.
Article 492: Where the People's Court considers it necessary, it may urge the parents or other guardians of a minor offender who is in prison to visit him or her in a timely manner.

Article 493: For minor offenders sentenced to public surveillance, granted probation, granted parole by ruling, or decided to be temporarily released on medical parole, the People's Court may assist the community correction institution in formulating measures for assistance and education.

Article 494: The People's Court may, at appropriate times, visit minor offenders who have been sentenced to public surveillance, granted probation, exempted from criminal punishment, granted parole by ruling, or decided to be temporarily released on medical parole, and their families, to learn about the management and education of the minor offenders, guide the families of minor offenders to assume the responsibility of discipline and education, and create a favorable environment for the minor offenders to reform.

Article 495: Where a minor offender sentenced to public surveillance, granted probation, exempted from criminal punishment, granted parole by ruling, or decided to be temporarily released on medical parole, meets the conditions for schooling or employment, the People's Court may submit a judicial recommendation to the relevant authorities regarding his or her placement and shall attach necessary materials.

Article 496: For a public prosecution case that meets the requirements of Article 277 of the Criminal Procedure Law, where the facts are clear and the evidence is sufficient, the People's Court shall inform the parties that they may voluntarily reach a settlement; where a party applies, the People's Court may preside over negotiations between the two parties to reach a settlement.
Based on the circumstances of the case, the People's Court may invite people's mediators, defenders, litigation agents, relatives and friends of the parties, and others to participate in facilitating a settlement between the two parties.

Article 497: For a public prosecution case that meets the requirements of Article 277 of the Criminal Procedure Law, where the victim dies, his or her close relatives may reach a settlement with the defendant. Where there are multiple close relatives, a settlement agreement shall be reached with the consent of all close relatives in the same inheritance order.
Where the victim is a person without or with limited capacity for civil conduct, his or her legal representative or close relatives may reach a settlement on his or her behalf.

Article 498: A close relative of the defendant may, with the consent of the defendant, reach a settlement on the defendant's behalf.
Where the defendant is a person with limited capacity for civil conduct, his or her legal representative may reach a settlement on the defendant's behalf.
Where the legal representative or close relative of the defendant reaches a settlement on the defendant's behalf in accordance with the preceding two paragraphs, the matters such as apology agreed upon in the settlement agreement shall be performed by the defendant personally.

Article 499: Where a party raises an objection to a settlement agreement prepared under the auspices of a public security organ or the People's Procuratorate, the People's Court shall review it. Upon review, if the settlement is voluntary and lawful, it shall be confirmed, and there shall be no need to prepare a new settlement agreement; if the settlement lacks voluntariness or lawfulness, it shall be deemed invalid. After the settlement agreement is deemed invalid, if the two parties subsequently reach a new settlement, the People's Court shall preside over the preparation of a new settlement agreement.

Article 500: During the trial period, where the two parties reach a settlement, the People's Court shall hear the opinions of the parties, their legal representatives, and other relevant persons. Where the two parties reach a settlement outside the court, the People's Court shall notify the People's Procuratorate and hear its opinions. Upon review, if the settlement is voluntary and lawful, the court shall preside over the preparation of a settlement agreement.

Article 501: A settlement agreement shall include the following:
(1) The defendant admits to the crime committed, has no objection to the criminal facts, and sincerely repents;
(2) The defendant obtains the victim's forgiveness by means such as apologizing and compensating for losses; where compensation for losses is involved, the amount and method of compensation shall be specified; where a collateral civil action has been initiated, the plaintiff in the collateral civil action shall withdraw the collateral civil action;
(3) The victim voluntarily settles and requests or agrees to a lenient punishment for the defendant according to law.
The settlement agreement shall be signed by both parties and the judicial personnel, but shall not be affixed with the seal of the People's Court.
The settlement agreement shall be made in triplicate, with each party holding one copy and the other copy submitted to the People's Court for attachment to the case file for future reference.
Where both parties request confidentiality of the compensation for losses content in the settlement agreement, the People's Court shall permit it and take corresponding confidentiality measures.

Article 502: The defendant shall perform the compensation for losses content agreed upon in the settlement agreement immediately after the agreement is signed.
Where the settlement agreement has been fully performed and a party reneges, the People's Court shall not support such reneging, unless there is evidence proving that the settlement violated the principles of voluntariness and lawfulness.

Article 503: Where the two parties have already reached a settlement agreement during the investigation or examination and prosecution stage and have fully performed it, and the victim or his or her legal representative or close relatives subsequently file a collateral civil action, the People's Court shall not accept it, unless there is evidence proving that the settlement violated the principles of voluntariness and lawfulness.

Article 504: Where, after the victim or his or her legal representative or close relatives have filed a collateral civil action, both parties are willing to settle, but the defendant cannot immediately perform the entire compensation obligation, the People's Court shall prepare a collateral civil mediation document.

Article 505: For a case where a settlement agreement has been reached, the People's Court shall give the defendant a lighter punishment; where the conditions for applying a non-custodial sentence are met, a non-custodial sentence shall be applied; where the statutory minimum punishment is still too severe, the punishment may be mitigated; where, based on a comprehensive review of the case, the circumstances of the crime are minor and no punishment is necessary, criminal punishment may be exempted.
In a joint crime case, where some defendants have reached a settlement agreement with the victim, those defendants may be given a lenient punishment according to law, but attention shall be paid to the balance of sentencing in the whole case.
Article 506: Where a settlement agreement is reached, the judgment document shall describe this and shall cite the relevant provisions of the Criminal Procedure Law.

Article 509: The property obtained from the commission of a criminal act and the proceeds thereof, as well as the prohibited articles illegally held by the defendant and the defendant's own property used for the crime, shall be considered "illegal gains and other property involved in the case" as specified in Article 280, paragraph 1, of the Criminal Procedure Law.

Article 513: A person who claims ownership of the property for which confiscation is applied shall be considered an "other interested party" as specified in Article 281, paragraph 2, of the Criminal Procedure Law.
Close relatives of the criminal suspect or defendant and other interested parties who apply to participate in the proceedings shall do so within the notice period. The close relatives of the criminal suspect or defendant shall provide evidentiary materials proving their relationship with the criminal suspect or defendant, and other interested parties shall provide evidentiary materials proving that the property for which confiscation is applied belongs to them.
Where close relatives of the criminal suspect or defendant and other interested parties apply to participate in the proceedings after the expiration of the notice period, if they can reasonably explain the reasons and provide evidentiary materials proving that the property for which confiscation is applied belongs to them, the People's Court shall permit such participation.

Article 514: After the expiration of the notice period, the People's Court shall form a collegial panel to hear the case concerning the application for confiscation of illegal gains.
Where an interested party applies to participate in the proceedings, the People's Court shall hold a court session. Where no interested party applies to participate in the proceedings, the court may hear the case without holding a court session.

Article 517: Where the criminal suspect, defendant's close relatives, and other interested parties or the People's Procuratorate disagree with the ruling on confiscation of illegal gains or dismissal of the application, they may file an appeal or protest within five days.

Article 519: During the trial of a case applying for confiscation of illegal gains, if the criminal suspect or defendant who is at large appears in court, the People's Court shall rule to terminate the trial. If the People's Procuratorate initiates a public prosecution before the People's Court that originally accepted the application, the same adjudication organization may try the case.

Article 520: During the trial of a case, if a defendant dies or escapes, meeting the conditions of Article 280, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Procedure Law, the People's Procuratorate may file an application for confiscation of illegal gains with the People's Court.
If the People's Procuratorate files an application with the People's Court that originally accepted the case, the same adjudication organization may try the case in accordance with the procedures provided in this Chapter.

Article 521: The time limit for trying a case applying for confiscation of illegal gains shall be subject to the trial time limits of the first instance ordinary procedure and the second instance procedure for public prosecution cases.
The period for announcement and the time for requesting criminal judicial assistance shall not be counted in the trial time limit.

Article 522: After the ruling on confiscation of illegal gains takes effect, if the criminal suspect or defendant appears in court and raises an objection to the confiscation ruling, and the People's Procuratorate initiates a public prosecution before the People's Court that originally made the ruling, the same adjudication organization may try the case.
After trial, the People's Court shall handle according to the following circumstances:
(1) If the original ruling is correct, it shall maintain it and no longer make a judgment on the property involved;
(2) If the original ruling is indeed erroneous, it shall revoke the original ruling and handle the relevant property involved together in the judgment.
If the effective confiscation ruling of the People's Court is indeed erroneous, except for the circumstances in paragraph 1, it shall be corrected in accordance with the trial supervision procedure. The property already confiscated shall be returned promptly; if the property has been turned over to the state treasury, the original confiscating organ shall apply to the financial authority for return of the funds and return them; if the original property has been sold or auctioned, the proceeds shall be returned; if property losses are caused to the criminal suspect, defendant, or interested parties, compensation shall be made according to law.

Article 523: For a case tried by the People's Court applying for confiscation of illegal gains, if this Chapter has no provisions, the relevant provisions of this Interpretation shall apply mutatis mutandis.

Article 524: A mentally ill person who commits violent acts, endangering public security or seriously endangering personal safety of citizens, whose social harmfulness has reached the level of a crime, but who, according to law, does not bear criminal liability due to mental illness as determined through legal procedures, and who is likely to continue to endanger society, may be subjected to compulsory medical treatment.

Article 525: A case where the People's Procuratorate applies for compulsory medical treatment of a mentally ill person who does not bear criminal liability according to law shall be under the jurisdiction of the Primary People's Court of the place where the respondent committed the violent act; if it is more appropriate for the People's Court of the respondent's domicile to adjudicate, the Primary People's Court of the respondent's domicile may have jurisdiction.

Article 528: When trying a compulsory medical treatment case, the People's Court shall notify the respondent or defendant's legal representative to be present. If the respondent or defendant has not retained a litigation agent, it shall notify a legal aid institution to appoint a lawyer to act as litigation agent and provide legal assistance.

Article 529: When trying a compulsory medical treatment case, the People's Court shall form a collegial panel and hold a trial in open court, except where the respondent or defendant's legal representative requests not to hold a trial in open court and the People's Court approves after examination.
When trying a case where the People's Procuratorate applies for compulsory medical treatment, the respondent shall be interviewed.

Article 532: If, during the trial of a case, the first instance People's Court discovers that the defendant may meet the conditions for compulsory medical treatment, it shall conduct a forensic psychiatric evaluation of the defendant in accordance with legal procedures. If, after evaluation, the defendant is found to be a mentally ill person who does not bear criminal liability according to law, the compulsory medical treatment procedure shall apply and the case shall be tried.
When holding a trial in open court for a case as provided in the preceding paragraph, the members of the collegial panel shall first read the forensic psychiatric evaluation opinion on the defendant, explaining that the defendant may meet the conditions for compulsory medical treatment, followed successively by the public prosecutor and the defendant's legal representative and litigation agent expressing opinions. With the permission of the presiding judge, the public prosecutor and the defendant's legal representative and litigation agent may debate.

Article 534: If, during the trial of a criminal case of second instance, the People's Court discovers that the defendant may meet the conditions for compulsory medical treatment, it may handle the case in accordance with the compulsory medical treatment procedure, or may rule to remand the case to the original trial People's Court for retrial.

Article 535: If the People's Court decides to impose compulsory medical treatment, it shall, within five days after making the decision, serve the compulsory medical treatment decision and the compulsory medical treatment execution notice on the public security organ, and the public security organ shall deliver the person subject to compulsory medical treatment to the compulsory medical institution.

Article 536: If the person subject to compulsory medical treatment, the victim, and their legal representatives or close relatives disagree with the compulsory medical treatment decision, they may, within five days from receipt of the decision, apply for reconsideration to the People's Court at the next higher level. During the period of reconsideration, the implementation of the compulsory medical treatment decision shall not be suspended.

Article 538: If, with respect to the judgment or decision as provided in item (1) of Article 533 of this Interpretation, the People's Procuratorate files a protest, and at the same time the person subject to compulsory medical treatment, the victim, and their legal representatives or close relatives apply for reconsideration, the People's Court at the next higher level shall handle the matter together in accordance with the second instance procedure.

Article 539: For trial of a compulsory medical treatment case, if this Chapter has no provisions, the relevant provisions of the first instance ordinary procedure and the second instance procedure for public prosecution cases shall apply mutatis mutandis.

Article 540: If the person subject to compulsory medical treatment or their close relatives apply for termination of compulsory medical treatment, they shall file the application with the People's Court that decided on the compulsory medical treatment.
If an application for termination of compulsory medical treatment filed by the person subject to compulsory medical treatment or their close relatives is dismissed by the People's Court, and the application is filed again six months later, the People's Court shall accept it.

Article 541: If the compulsory medical treatment institution submits an opinion on termination of compulsory medical treatment, or if the person subject to compulsory medical treatment or their close relatives apply for termination of compulsory medical treatment, the People's Court shall examine whether a diagnostic evaluation report on the person subject to compulsory medical treatment is attached.
If the compulsory medical treatment institution submits an opinion on termination of compulsory medical treatment without attaching a diagnostic evaluation report, the People's Court shall require it to provide one.
If the person subject to compulsory medical treatment or their close relatives apply to the People's Court for termination of compulsory medical treatment and the compulsory medical treatment institution has not provided a diagnostic evaluation report, the applicant may apply to the People's Court to obtain it. When necessary, the People's Court may entrust an evaluation institution to evaluate the person subject to compulsory medical treatment.

Article 542: If the compulsory medical treatment institution submits an opinion on termination of compulsory medical treatment, or if the person subject to compulsory medical treatment or their close relatives apply for termination of compulsory medical treatment, the People's Court shall form a collegial panel to conduct examination and, within one month, handle according to the following circumstances:
(1) If the person subject to compulsory medical treatment no longer poses a personal danger and does not need continued compulsory medical treatment, it shall make a decision to terminate compulsory medical treatment and may order the family members of the person subject to compulsory medical treatment to keep strict custody and provide medical treatment;
(2) If the person subject to compulsory medical treatment still poses a personal danger and needs continued compulsory medical treatment, it shall make a decision to continue compulsory medical treatment.
The People's Court shall, within five days after making the decision, serve the decision on the compulsory medical treatment institution, the applicant for termination of compulsory medical treatment, the person subject to compulsory medical treatment, and the People's Procuratorate. If the decision is to terminate compulsory medical treatment, it shall notify the compulsory medical treatment institution to terminate compulsory medical treatment on the day of receipt of the decision.

Article 543: If the People's Procuratorate considers that the compulsory medical treatment decision or the decision to terminate compulsory medical treatment is improper and submits a written correction opinion within 20 days after receipt of the decision, the People's Court shall form a separate collegial panel to try the case and make a decision within one month.

Article 544: When the People's Court interrogates a defendant, announces a judgment, or tries a case of commutation of punishment or parole, it may adopt a video method based on the circumstances of the case.

Article 545: Any submission of a private prosecution, appeal, petition, or application to the People's Court shall be made in writing. If the person has difficulty in writing, unless otherwise provided, it may be made orally, and the People's Court staff shall make notes or record it in the case file and read it to or let the oral declarant read it.

Article 546: Work records, notification records, and other materials produced or formed during the litigation period shall be signed and sealed by the producers and other relevant persons. When serving or announcing litigation documents such as judgments, rulings, decisions, and notices, the person receiving the service or announcement shall sign and seal the litigation documents or the service receipt.
If a litigation participant fails to sign and seal, they shall affix a fingerprint; in addition to signing and sealing, a criminal defendant shall also affix a fingerprint.
If a party refuses to sign, seal, or affix a fingerprint, the case-handling personnel shall note the circumstances in the litigation documents or records, and if there are relevant witnesses to witness, or if there is audio or video recording evidence, it shall not affect the validity of the relevant litigation documents or records.
Article 547: The relevant provisions of this Interpretation apply to special People's Courts such as the Military Courts and the Railway Transport Courts.

Article 548: This Interpretation shall come into force as of January 1, 2013. The Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China issued by the Supreme People's Court on September 2, 1998 shall be abolished simultaneously; where judicial interpretations and normative documents previously issued by the Supreme People's Court are inconsistent with this Interpretation, this Interpretation shall prevail.
